mp3\\beat-B00.mp3: Ciao, this is Liam in for bear. Zhao Hui Li's Dusk Duel is a 2D fighting game. Assignment 5 adds two shaders Zhao Hui typed by hand. A red flash on whichever fighter was just hit and a granite surface in the 3D prop room. Claude wrote the driver, the tests, and the audit. This film follows what the tests proved and what only eyes could judge.
mp3\\beat-B01.mp3: Two shaders typed by hand. The headless tests prove they parse and that they're driven and wired as the brief said. Not that they look right, that part needed eyes.
mp3\\beat-B02.mp3: Here's the game, Akakan punches, and Aro Take turns red for about a third of a second, then fades back. A moment later Aro Take kicks, and this time only Akakan flashes.
mp3\\beat-B03.mp3: Before either shader existed, the brief named the color line makes each pixel's own color toward red by hert amount. From that one line, Zhao Hui worked out by hand what two pixels of Akakan become at zero, a half in one, the orange ghee, and the pale hand wrap.
mp3\\beat-B04.mp3: So what is a shader? A small program the graphics card runs for every pixel of this sprite all at once. Line 1 makes it a canvas item shader for 2D. Lines 3 and 4 are uniforms. Values the game can set. Line 7 is the color line, mixing the pixels color toward the flash color.
mp3\\beat-B05.mp3: Here's line 7's output, captured from the running engine with the value set from code. Every sampled pixel lands within one step of Zhao Hui's arithmetic. The steady one step shortfall is the sprite's alpha, 254, not 255.
mp3\\beat-B06.mp3: A shader remembers nothing, so game state has to arrive as a uniform. This driver is Claude's. Lines 19 to 21 give each fighter its own material. The material holds the values the shader is shared. Line 27 reads the stun counter once per physics tick, so the flash lasts 22 ticks at any frame rate.
mp3\\beat-B07.mp3: That's why when Arotake's kick lands, only Akakan flashes. One shader, two materials, two different values of her to mount.
mp3\\beat-B08.mp3: Zhao Hui predicted that Hint range would not clamp a value set from code. With the red flash you can't tell, 1 and 2 both saturate. With Gray 2 gives 34, 167, the mix extrapolated not clamped, the prediction held.
mp3\\beat-B09.mp3: The headless test drives the real game loop with the J key and samples the value every frame at 30, 60, and 144 frames per second. Its first run failed for checks, a second hit can't land during hurt in real play, and time scale doesn't slow the fight. Jau-H-way revised the brief, not the assertions, now 69 pass at every rate.
mp3\\beat-B10.mp3: Then Zhao Hui broke the shaders on purpose. A missing semicolon, the uniform list comes back empty. A renamed uniform still parses, and all 23 behavior checks still pass, because setting a name the shader doesn't have raises no error. Only the uniform list noticed, deleting source color fails the material test.
mp3\\beat-B11.mp3: Now a texture, why is it information, not a picture? Lines three to five are three files of numbers. Line three says source color. These numbers are colored to code them. Line four has no such hint. Roughness read is stored. Line five marks a normal map. The uniforms below are inspector controls in two groups.
mp3\\beat-B12.mp3: Two materials share that shader, the floor at UV Scale 6, the plinth at 1, tinted the A3 Stone color. Change one value in one material and only the floor changes. Edit one shader line, Zhao Hui checked and both change. And Zhao Hui's verdict on the granite, it looks like wooden planks. The box UVS stretch it.
mp3\\beat-B13.mp3: Each uniform swept to its ends, UV scale changes the grain, roughness and normal strength change how the light sits on it, and tint at black and jow each way's words isn't good looking.
mp3\\beat-B14.mp3: The hint experiment asks what a hint does to the number the shader receives. One 3-pixel file, grays 64, 128, and 192. Line 4 reads it with source color, line 5 without. The bull on line 7 picks which one writes albedo on an unshaded quad.
mp3\\beat-B15.mp3: Zhao Hui predicted Quad B would brighten to 137, 188, and 224. Both quads show the stored values. In Godot's compatibility renderer, every albedo is decoded, whatever the hint, then encoded on output. The prediction followed the forward plus pipeline. This project had to measure first.
mp3\\beat-B16.mp3: And what is the Godot shading language? Close to GLSL, but you pick a shader type instead of writing main and hints shape the inspector. Here's the shader Godot generated for standard material beside Zhao Hui's, the Albedo lines match. The normal map uses hint roughness normal, which in the editor also feeds the roughness import.
mp3\\beat-B17.mp3: So what did the tests prove that the shaders parse that their uniforms are declared and driven and that the materials are wired even from an empty cache? Not how anything looks. Those are jow-h-way's checks and jow-h-way's words. The flash can be seen, the quads are alike, the granite looks like wood. The screenshot comparison wasn't done.
mp3\\beat-B18.mp3: Verdict checked 69 checks at three frame rates, 96 material checks from an empty cache, three mutations that fail, and pixels within one step of the hand predictions. Uncertain, the retrigger is reachable only by test setup, and the screenshot comparison wasn't done. Claude got four things wrong, an outdated command line tool, null material values, captures sampled at the wrong scale, and a wrong claim about hint normal. Zhao Hui typed every shader line, predicted broke and judged them. Claude wrote the driver, the tests, the audit, and the captures. Next step, a UV scale per axis, so the granite stops looking like planks.
